rationale: This is a numerator swap inside the already-evaluated "Dilution-Adjusted Operating Improvement" construct (oiadp → oibdp−xint), explicitly motivated by splicing the fmb t-stat of one archived signal onto the alpha of another rather than by a new mechanism, which is precisely the cosmetic-variant metric-chasing to avoid.

It simply replaces the second leg of the archived "Fixed-Claim Per-Share Erosion" with the archived dilution-adjusted improvement block, and since the (xint+dvt)/at multiplier is nonnegative the signal is essentially a fixed-claim-weighted re-scaling of an already-tested factor, not a new economic conditioning story.

This is structurally identical to the archived "Innovation Dilution-Adjusted Conversion" with xsga−xrd substituted for xrd in the ranking leg, i.e., a rediscovery of an already-evaluated template with an interchangeable intangible-intensity proxy.

It shares the MUL(dltis/at, IND_ADJ((X−xint)/at)) skeleton of the archived "Debt Issue Coverage Strain," but substituting noncash depreciation for operating profit changes the economics to a tangibility/tax-shield debt-capacity story that is genuinely distinct and internally consistent, though the leg is close to a mechanical capital-intensity proxy and the mechanism is only loosely linked to expected returns.

This is the fifth iteration of the archive's "dividend intensity × deteriorating condition" family (cash erosion, margin erosion, maturity gap, cash volatility), all of which delivered weak Fama-MacBeth slopes, and Δ(xint/at) is largely a mechanical restatement of debt growth rather than a distinct conditioning variable.

It is a plug-and-play recombination of two already-evaluated components (the internal-funding rank leg from "Self-Funded Innovation/Organizational Capital" and the per-share after-interest growth leg), and GROWTH of the possibly-negative quantity (oibdp−xint)/csho is poorly behaved, making the signed outcome leg unreliable near zero profits.
